title: The Name field's @ prefix cannot be removed or clicked into
custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Owner/Admin user.
  • The Notifications page is open on the Tag groups tab.
  • An active location is selected.
  • The New tag group dialog is open (and later the Edit tag group dialog).
custom_steps:
1. Read the fixed @ at the left edge of the Name field, before the typing area, in both New and Edit dialogs.
  2. Try to select, delete, type over or cut the @; press Home and hold the left arrow; use Select All.
  3. Note the @'s colour and the separator between it and the typing area.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • The Name field carries a fixed @ at its left edge, before the typing area, always shown in both New and Edit dialogs.
  • The @ cannot be removed - it cannot be selected, deleted, typed over or cut; the caret sits after it whenever the field has focus (including on Home or holding left arrow), and Select All selects only the typed text.
  • The @ reads as part of the field: it is shown in the field's secondary text colour with a hairline rule separating it from the typing area, and the typed value keeps the ordinary input colour and weight.

Source - where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-9667; story SV-10249 (S6, Manage tag groups); Notifications Update v1 PRD (Confluence 817463297), S6; design boards TagGroups/Modal; read 30 Sep 2026. Source-verified 30 September 2026.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S6-R8a: “The Name field carries a fixed @ at its left edge, before the typing area. It is always shown, in the New tag group dialog and in the Edit tag group dialog alike.”
  • S6-R8b: “The @ cannot be removed. It cannot be selected, deleted, typed over, or cut. The caret sits after it whenever the field has focus, including when the user presses Home or holds the left arrow, and Select All selects only the typed text.”
  • S6-R8c: “The @ reads as part of the field rather than as a character the user typed. It is shown in the field's secondary text color rather than the color of the typed value, and a hairline rule separates it from the typing area. The typed value keeps the ordinary input color and weight.”

Last checked against build v26.40.7-7ffda69 on 10/5/2026.
